title: Quiet money (batch 8): quiet data-broker & cyber-surveillance fortunes
source: Public record: company histories; SEC filings (Wiz/Google 2025, Cellebrite CLBT, Verint/Cognyte); Forbes/Bloomberg; LexisNexis Risk/Seisint/TLO histories; Citizen Lab + press on the commercial-surveillance market. Catalog layer (#242 batch 8). Structural overlay; person nodes carry dossiers. FOCUS: low-profile fortunes built ON the data-broker, forensics, and surveillance-analytics economy the rest of the map documents. HONESTY: founder roles/ownership/deals = fact; specific surveillance-use + intent framings graded; no cabal imputed.

edges.notes: Assaf Rappaport (ex-Microsoft cloud-security GM; earlier sold Adallom to Microsoft) co-founded Wiz - the fastest-growing cloud-security firm; a low-profile Israeli cyber fortune (fact).
2025: Google/Alphabet agreed to acquire Wiz for ~$32B - one of the largest cybersecurity deals ever, folding a quiet Israeli security firm into Big Tech (fact; deal under regulatory review).
Wiz secures cloud + AI infrastructure (agentless scanning, AI-pipeline security) - wiring the quiet cyber-money layer to the AI-buildout thread (fact of product scope).

Shiv Nadar - one of India's quietest tech magnates - founded HCL, now HCLTech, a global IT-services + engineering giant; a large, low-profile fortune + major philanthropist (Shiv Nadar Foundation) (fact).
HCLTech is a pillar of India's IT-services export economy - managing infrastructure, data, and applications for global corporations + governments (fact).
HCLTech (like TCS/Infosys/Wipro) runs enterprise data + AI/automation services at scale - the quiet back-office layer of the global data economy (fact of category).

Hank Asher (d. 2013) - the 'father of data fusion' - built Seisint (whose Accurint + the post-9/11 MATRIX program tied together public + private records) which became the core of LexisNexis Risk; later founded TLO (-> TransUnion) - a quiet, controversial data-broker fortune (fact).

Asher's data-fusion model - merging consumer, government, and behavioral records for search by law enforcement - is a foundational template for the modern commercial-surveillance stack (fact of technique; broader impact graded).

Jacob 'Kobi' Alexander founded Comverse Technology, whose Verint unit became a leading surveillance-analytics + lawful-intercept vendor; Alexander fled a US options-backdating indictment to Namibia, later returned + pleaded guilty (2016) - a quiet, tarnished surveillance-tech fortune (fact).

Verint supplies communications-interception, monitoring, and analytics to governments, telcos, and enterprises worldwide - core plumbing of the lawful-intercept + surveillance-analytics market (fact; specific-country deployments graded).

Verint spun off Cognyte (2021) as its dedicated investigative-analytics ('security analytics') arm - Cognyte flagged in commercial-spyware/surveillance reporting; the corporate lineage of the surveillance-analytics business (fact).
Cellebrite's phone-extraction/forensics tools are procured by US agencies including ICE/HSI + DHS - mobile-device unlocking embedded in immigration + criminal enforcement (fact).

Cellebrite (public: CLBT) sells UFED/Physical Analyzer to thousands of police + government agencies globally - the dominant lawful phone-forensics vendor; recurring civil-liberties + due-process debate over scope (fact of market; use-abuse framing graded).
